title: Greek Yogurt vs Regular Yogurt: Protein, Fat and Sugar

seo.title: Greek vs Regular Yogurt: Protein, Fat and Sugar
seo.meta_description: Plain Greek yogurt often has 8–10 g protein/100 g versus 3–5 g in regular yogurt. Fat depends on milkfat level, and added sugar can outweigh style differences.
seo.search_intent: Compare Greek and regular yogurt without confusing straining with milkfat level or added sugar.

excerpt: Plain Greek yogurt usually contains about twice as much protein as conventional plain yogurt, roughly 8–10 grams versus 3–5 grams per 100 grams. But “Greek” does not automatically mean more fat or less sugar: those depend on milkfat level, processing and whether sweeteners were added.
content_html:
Greek and regular yogurt are often compared as if “Greek” automatically meant higher fat and “regular” automatically meant lower sugar. That mixes three separate questions: how concentrated the yogurt is, what milkfat level it uses and whether sweeteners were added afterward.

The most consistent difference is protein: strained Greek yogurt usually provides about twice as much for the same weight. For fat and sugar, the style name alone is not enough.

A useful comparison of plain whole-milk versions

Per 100 gPlain regular yogurtPlain Greek yogurt
Calories~60–65~90–100
Protein~3.5–4 g~8–10 g
Fat~3–3.5 g~4–5 g
Natural sugars~4.5–5 g~3–4 g

The protein gap is substantial. In a 6-ounce serving, Greek yogurt can provide roughly 15–17 grams of protein, while the same weight of conventional plain yogurt is closer to 6–7 grams.

Why Greek yogurt concentrates more protein

Traditional Greek yogurt is strained to remove part of the whey. Water and some dissolved lactose leave with it, so the remaining yogurt becomes more concentrated.

No new protein is created by straining. One hundred grams of the finished food simply contains less water and therefore more milk solids.

Fat depends mainly on whether it is whole, low-fat or nonfat

Whole Greek yogurt can contain around 5 grams of fat per 100 grams, while nonfat Greek yogurt can fall below 1 gram. Regular yogurt works the same way: whole versions may have around 3–4 grams and nonfat versions almost none.

Comparing whole Greek yogurt with nonfat regular yogurt and concluding that Greek yogurt is inherently much fattier would attribute a milkfat difference to the yogurt style.

Plain Greek yogurt often contains a little less lactose

Because some lactose leaves with the whey, plain Greek yogurt can land around 3–4 grams of sugar per 100 grams versus roughly 4.5–5 grams in regular yogurt.

That difference is real but small. Added sugar, honey, syrup or fruit preparations can have a much larger effect: some flavored yogurts exceed 10–15 grams of total sugar per 100 grams.

“No added sugar” does not mean “no sugar”

Milk naturally contains lactose. A yogurt with no added sugar will still list several grams of total sugar on the Nutrition Facts label; those grams are not automatically added table sugar.

Calcium does not always favor Greek yogurt

Some calcium can leave with the whey during certain straining processes, so conventional yogurt may provide more calcium per serving than some Greek products. Formulas vary widely by brand, which makes the label especially useful here.

What to check at the store

If protein is the priority, compare grams per 100 grams or per container. If fat matters, look at the milkfat level. And if you want to minimize added sugar, check the ingredient list and added-sugars line when available.

Greek yogurt is a very efficient way to concentrate protein; regular yogurt can fit just as well when that is not the goal. The style name is useful context, but it does not replace the nutrition label.

faq.question: Which has more protein, Greek or regular yogurt?
faq.answer: Greek yogurt usually provides about 8–10 g/100 g versus roughly 3–5 g/100 g in conventional plain yogurt.

faq.question: Is Greek yogurt higher in fat?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. It depends on whether the product is whole, low-fat or nonfat; fat-free Greek yogurts are common.

faq.question: Which has less sugar?
faq.answer: Plain Greek yogurt often contains a little less lactose. In flavored products, added sugar can matter far more than that difference.
